title: Polynomial-time planted-clique detection below the square-root scale
open: Determine whether a randomized polynomial-time algorithm can distinguish \(G(n,1/2)\) from the same graph with a planted clique of size \(\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\), with error tending to zero.
status: A longstanding average-case complexity problem. Exhaustive search succeeds well below the regime reached by standard polynomial-time methods; planted-clique assumptions support numerous conditional statistical lower bounds.
why: A resolution would change computational feasibility claims across high-dimensional statistics.
key_works: Berthet and Rigollet, 2013, “Complexity Theoretic Lower Bounds for Sparse Principal Component Detection,” PMLR 30; Brennan, Bresler, and Huleihel, 2018, “Reducibility and Computational Lower Bounds for Problems with Planted Sparse Structure,” arXiv:1806.07508.

title: Complete computational minimax frontier for sparse PCA
open: Characterize the best polynomial-time estimation risk for a sparse leading eigenvector across sample size, ambient dimension, sparsity, and signal strength, including transition regimes rather than only separated asymptotic cases.
status: Information-theoretic rates, efficient algorithms, and conditional hardness results cover substantial regions. A single sharp computational risk characterization, including boundary behavior and constants, remains a research target.
why: It would identify when additional data can substitute for unavailable computation.
key_works: Berthet and Rigollet, 2013, “Complexity Theoretic Lower Bounds for Sparse Principal Component Detection”; Brennan, Bresler, and Huleihel, 2018, “Reducibility and Computational Lower Bounds for Problems with Planted Sparse Structure,” arXiv:1806.07508.

title: Tensor PCA below known efficient thresholds
open: For a rank-one order-three tensor in Gaussian noise, determine the smallest signal allowing polynomial-time weak recovery, and whether the information–computation gap is intrinsic.
status: The gap has been studied since at least 2014. Information-theoretic recovery and available algorithmic guarantees operate at different signal scales; computational conclusions depend on the algorithm class or hardness hypothesis.
why: It would clarify the limits of higher-order latent-variable estimation.
key_works: Montanari and Richard, 2014, “A statistical model for tensor PCA,” arXiv:1411.1076.

title: Submatrix detection with uncertain heterogeneous noise
open: Derive matching statistical and computational detection boundaries for an unknown elevated-mean rectangle when entry variances are heterogeneous and estimated from limited auxiliary observations.
status: Research target extending the established homogeneous submatrix model. Classical computational barriers do not by themselves characterize the interaction between variance-estimation error, rectangular sparsity, and signal strength.
why: It would make biclustering guarantees relevant to unevenly measured biological and industrial data.
key_works: Ma and Wu, 2015, “Computational barriers in minimax submatrix detection,” arXiv:1309.5914, DOI:10.1214/14-AOS1300.

title: Universality for correlated non-Gaussian designs
open: Find verifiable dependence conditions under which precise high-dimensional risk formulas remain universal when design entries are correlated and non-Gaussian.
status: Universality is established for important independent-entry settings; arbitrary isotropic designs admit counterexamples. The open problem is a useful intermediate class with sharp assumptions.
why: It would justify Gaussian-derived predictions for realistic structured data.
key_works: Han and Shen, 2023, “Universality of regularized regression estimators in high dimensions,” arXiv:2206.07936, DOI:10.1214/23-AOS2309.

title: Confidence sets through eigenvalue collisions
open: Construct honest confidence sets that adapt between identifiable individual eigenvectors and only-identifiable invariant subspaces as population eigengaps shrink at unknown rates.
status: Spectral-projector normal approximations provide a substantial baseline. Uniform inference across merging eigenvalues requires handling a changing identifiable parameter.
why: It would prevent falsely precise principal-component interpretations near degeneracy.
key_works: Koltchinskii and Lounici, 2017, “Normal approximation and concentration of spectral projectors of sample covariance,” arXiv:1504.07333, DOI:10.1214/16-AOS1437.

title: Logistic-regression inference near the separation transition
open: Derive finite-size scaling laws and uniformly valid inference when high-dimensional logistic regression approaches the boundary between existence and nonexistence of the maximum-likelihood estimator.
status: Modern proportional-asymptotic theory describes major departures from classical likelihood theory. The critical window and practical uncertainty statements across it remain a sharper target.
why: It would identify when familiar coefficient estimates become fundamentally unstable.
key_works: Sur and Candès, 2019, “A modern maximum-likelihood theory for high-dimensional logistic regression,” arXiv:1803.06964, DOI:10.1073/pnas.1810420116.

title: Standard-assumption hardness for bounded-moment robust means
open: Establish computational lower bounds, under broadly accepted assumptions, separating information-theoretic robust mean rates under bounded fourth or higher directional moments from polynomial-time achievable rates.
status: Hardness results and algorithms depend strongly on whether moment conditions are merely true or efficiently certifiable. The distinction remains central in the 2025 open-problem discussion.
why: It would explain whether weaker modeling assumptions necessarily cost computational efficiency.
key_works: Hopkins and Li, 2019, “How hard is robust mean estimation?” arXiv:1903.07870; UW CSE 599K, 2025, “Lecture 18.”

title: The sparse robust-mean sample gap
open: Close the gap between information-theoretic and polynomial-time sample requirements for estimating a sparse mean under adversarial contamination, or prove a sharp computational barrier.
status: Efficient methods can require substantially worse sparsity dependence than unrestricted estimators. Ordinary sparse estimation and ordinary robust estimation do not settle their combination.
why: It would support reliable feature discovery in contaminated high-dimensional data.
key_works: Georgiev and Hopkins, 2022, “Privacy Induces Robustness: Information-Computation Gaps and Sparse Mean Estimation,” arXiv:2211.00724; Hopkins and Li, 2019, “How hard is robust mean estimation?”

title: Simultaneous graph inference under cellwise contamination
open: Construct simultaneous confidence statements for a sparse precision matrix when individual cells, rather than entire observations, are corrupted and contamination rates vary across coordinates.
status: Robust precision-matrix estimation under cellwise contamination has a 2015 baseline. Selection-valid edge inference and sharp uncertainty under heterogeneous contamination are stronger targets.
why: It would make corrupted laboratory and sensor tables usable for network discovery.
key_works: Loh and Tan, 2015, “High-dimensional robust precision matrix estimation: Cellwise corruption under ε-contamination,” arXiv:1509.07229.

title: Adaptive bands with unknown anisotropic self-similarity
open: Construct honest, rate-adaptive confidence bands for anisotropic functions when smoothness differs by coordinate and the constants controlling self-similarity are unknown.
status: Honest adaptation is impossible over unrestricted nested smoothness classes; self-similarity permits positive results. The target is the sharp attainable anisotropic and locally varying extension.
why: It would permit uncertainty bands that adapt without hiding uncheckable tuning choices.
key_works: Bull, 2012, “Honest adaptive confidence bands and self-similar functions,” arXiv:1110.4985, DOI:10.1214/12-EJS720.

title: Confidence sets adapting to intrinsic dimension
open: Determine which separation and geometric conditions permit confidence sets to adapt simultaneously to unknown smoothness, manifold dimension, and support geometry.
status: Adaptation results exist for fixed-dimensional function and distribution classes. Unknown geometry introduces additional indistinguishability boundaries that require explicit treatment.
why: It would justify dimension-adaptive uncertainty rather than only dimension-adaptive prediction.
key_works: Deo and Randrianarisoa, 2021, “On Adaptive Confidence Sets for the Wasserstein Distances,” arXiv:2111.08505; Bull, 2012, “Honest adaptive confidence bands and self-similar functions.”

title: Adaptive conditional-independence testing
open: Derive minimax testing rates and adaptive procedures for conditional independence over classes with unknown smoothness, sparse relevant conditioning variables, and explicitly bounded conditional densities.
status: Unrestricted conditional-independence testing has strong impossibility results. The open task is to identify sharp, useful restricted classes and the cost of adapting among them.
why: It would strengthen causal discovery and conditional association screening.
key_works: Shah and Peters, 2020, “The Hardness of Conditional Independence Testing and the Generalised Covariance Measure,” arXiv:1804.07203, DOI:10.1214/19-AOS1857.

title: Power-optimal testing after learning the test representation
open: Design two-sample tests that learn kernels or representations from the tested observations while retaining finite-sample error control and near-oracle power over specified alternative classes.
status: Sample splitting and adaptive-data-analysis techniques provide valid approaches. The sharper target is the best achievable power–reuse tradeoff, rather than validity alone.
why: It would reduce the substantial power losses caused by reserving data for representation learning.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Wasserman, Ramdas, and Balakrishnan, 2020, “Universal Inference,” arXiv:1912.11436.

title: Entropy-rate estimation with unknown memory and mixing
open: Determine minimax rates for entropy-rate estimation when the process has unknown finite memory and unknown mixing strength, with procedures adapting to both.
status: Sharp results exist for important stationary reversible Markov-chain classes. Unknown memory, growing state spaces, and adaptation across mixing regimes are a distinct extension.
why: It would improve principled complexity measurement for language, biological sequences, and telemetry.
key_works: Han, Jiao, Lee, Weissman, Wu, and Yu, 2018, “Entropy Rate Estimation for Markov Chains with Large State Space,” arXiv:1802.07889.

title: Sharp risk of smoothed log-concave estimators
open: Determine sharp global and local risk guarantees for smoothed log-concave maximum-likelihood estimators, including whether smoothing preserves optimal adaptation to simpler densities.
status: Smoothed estimators have existed since at least 2013. Their practical usefulness is ahead of a complete sharp risk theory.
why: It would justify smooth density and tail estimates rather than treating smoothing as a cosmetic step.
key_works: Chen and Samworth, 2013, “Smoothed log-concave maximum likelihood estimation with applications,” arXiv:1102.1191, DOI:10.5705/ss.2011.224.

title: Remaining logarithmic gaps in log-concave density risk
open: Remove unnecessary logarithmic factors, or prove their necessity, in global Hellinger-risk bounds for multivariate log-concave maximum-likelihood estimation.
status: Dimension-dependent polynomial rates are known. The recent survey identifies remaining logarithmic discrepancies rather than an absence of minimax theory.
why: It would complete one of shape-constrained statistics’ central benchmark problems.
key_works: Kim and Samworth, 2016, “Global rates of convergence in log-concave density estimation,” arXiv:1404.2298, DOI:10.1214/16-AOS1480.

title: Certificates of unexplored posterior mass
subfield: Markov-chain Monte Carlo and posterior computation
open: Under explicit geometric assumptions on separated modes, construct computable upper bounds on posterior mass that a finite collection of chains may have missed.
status: Standard convergence diagnostics cannot certify arbitrary undiscovered modes. The open target is useful certification under stated restrictions, not an impossible universal diagnostic.
why: It would prevent seemingly converged chains from supporting confidently wrong decisions.
key_works: Vehtari et al., 2021, “Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC,” arXiv:1903.08008.

title: Complexity theory for practical NUTS
subfield: Markov-chain Monte Carlo and posterior computation
open: Prove end-to-end sampling complexity for realistically adapted No-U-Turn samplers, including step-size adaptation, mass-matrix learning, trajectory termination, and constrained parameter transformations.
status: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo has a substantial theoretical foundation; practical adaptive implementations combine mechanisms whose full guarantees require additional assumptions and analysis.
why: It would explain when a standard Bayesian workhorse can be trusted to scale.
key_works: Betancourt, 2017, “A Conceptual Introduction to Hamiltonian Monte Carlo,” arXiv:1701.02434.

title: Computable functional-bias bounds for variational inference
open: Produce useful, computable bounds on errors in selected posterior expectations and tail probabilities from a fitted variational approximation, without requiring the exact posterior normalizing constant.
status: Variational objectives are tractable surrogates, but objective quality alone does not guarantee every scientific functional is accurate.
why: It would convert fast approximations into auditable inferential tools.
key_works: Blei, Kucukelbir, and McAuliffe, 2017, “Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians,” arXiv:1601.00670, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2017.1285773.

title: Complete admissibility theory for e-processes
open: Give necessary and sufficient conditions for admissibility of e-processes under broad composite nulls, including when one process uniformly improves another.
status: Martingale-based necessity results are established; the 2023 safe-inference survey lists broader admissibility questions.
why: It would distinguish fundamentally efficient sequential evidence from avoidable conservatism.
key_works: Ramdas, Ruf, Larsson, and Koolen, 2020, “Admissible anytime-valid sequential inference must rely on nonnegative martingales,” arXiv:2009.03167.

title: Sharp power theory for universal inference
open: Characterize the best achievable power and confidence-set size for universal-inference constructions, including optimal splitting, aggregation, and nuisance fitting.
status: Finite-sample validity is established for broad likelihood-based settings. Sharp efficiency relative to model-specific procedures remains the stronger target.
why: It would show when broad applicability costs little and when it is prohibitively conservative.
key_works: Wasserman, Ramdas, and Balakrishnan, 2020, “Universal Inference,” arXiv:1912.11436.

title: Model-X inference with learned covariate distributions
open: Obtain sharp false-discovery guarantees when the covariate distribution used to construct knockoffs is learned imperfectly, with uncertainty that adapts to where misspecification matters.
status: Model-X knockoffs provide guarantees under appropriate distributional knowledge. Robustness to estimated conditional laws is an active extension, not an automatic consequence.
why: It would make conditional variable discovery less dependent on an unverifiable generative model.
key_works: Candès, Fan, Janson, and Lv, 2018, “Panning for Gold: Model-X Knockoffs for High-dimensional Controlled Variable Selection,” arXiv:1610.02351.

title: Error control for adaptively constructed hypothesis hierarchies
open: Control false discoveries simultaneously across levels when the hierarchy of groups and subgroups is learned from the same data used for testing.
status: Research target combining structured testing and adaptive analysis. A fixed hierarchy is materially simpler than one chosen to make discoveries look coherent.
why: It would support reliable pathway, ontology, and subgroup discovery.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Wang and Ramdas, 2022, “False discovery rate control with e-values.”

title: Selective inference after deep clustering
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Derive valid uncertainty for differences between clusters produced by a learned nonlinear representation, including selection of architecture, cluster count, and comparison.
status: Exact selective methods exist for tractable selection events. Deep clustering generally produces a much more complicated data-dependent event.
why: It would prevent algorithmically manufactured groups from generating spurious scientific findings.
key_works: Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference, with application to the lasso,” arXiv:1311.6238; Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis.”

title: Inference over analyst-selected multiverses
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Quantify uncertainty when analysts explore many defensible specifications and choose which subset to report, without assuming the explored set was fixed in advance.
status: Many-analyst studies demonstrate substantial analytic variability. The target is valid inference for adaptive exploration, not merely displaying a specification curve.
why: It would make robustness analysis resistant to its own selection bias.
key_works: Botvinik-Nezer et al., 2020, “Variability in the analysis of a single neuroimaging dataset by many teams,” DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2314-9; Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis.”

title: Cross-validation uncertainty under weak algorithmic stability
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Construct informative confidence intervals for prediction risk after cross-validation-based model selection under explicitly weak stability and dependence assumptions.
status: There is no universally unbiased estimator of K-fold cross-validation variance. That negative result does not settle restricted, calibrated intervals for modern unstable learners.
why: It would make reported differences between predictive models more trustworthy.
key_works: Bengio and Grandvalet, 2004, “No Unbiased Estimator of the Variance of K-Fold Cross-Validation,” JMLR 5:1089–1105.

title: Conditional coverage versus prediction-set size
open: Determine sharp achievable tradeoffs among approximate conditional coverage, the complexity of the conditioning family, and expected prediction-set volume.
status: Exact unrestricted distribution-free conditional coverage is already ruled out in useful settings. The open problem concerns nontrivial restricted or approximate guarantees.
why: It would clarify what “reliable for people like this” can actually mean.
key_works: Barber, Candès, Ramdas, and Tibshirani, 2019/2021, “The limits of distribution-free conditional predictive inference,” arXiv:1903.04684.

title: Conformal prediction with uncertain shift weights
open: Construct sharp finite-sample coverage bounds when covariate-shift importance weights are estimated, potentially misspecified, and unstable in low-overlap regions.
status: Weighted and doubly robust calibration methods exist. The target is a complete finite-sample uncertainty accounting for the weights themselves.
why: It would improve prediction after deployment populations change.
key_works: Yang, Kuchibhotla, and Tchetgen Tchetgen, 2024, “Doubly robust calibration of prediction sets under covariate shift,” JRSS B 86:943–965; Barber et al., 2023, “Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability,” arXiv:2202.13415.

title: Minimal validation designs for causal measurement error
open: Determine which combinations of repeated measurements, validation subsamples, and randomized measurement devices identify causal effects when errors are nonlinear and correlated.
status: Proxy-variable identification supplies useful special cases. A design-level characterization for dependent errors is a more specific outstanding target.
why: It would tell investigators what extra measurements are actually worth collecting.
key_works: Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen, 2018, “Identifying causal effects with proxy variables of an unmeasured confounder”; Tchetgen Tchetgen et al., 2020, “An Introduction to Proximal Causal Learning,” arXiv:2009.10982.

title: Heterogeneous-effect inference under weak overlap
open: Derive minimax confidence bands for conditional treatment effects when overlap deteriorates with sample size and effect smoothness is unknown.
status: Flexible treatment-effect estimation is mature in important regimes. Uniform uncertainty, bias adaptation, and weak overlap interact in ways not settled by prediction rates alone.
why: It would identify which personalized treatment recommendations are supported by data.
key_works: Cinelli et al., 2025, “Challenges in Statistics: A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference,” arXiv:2508.17099; Bull, 2012, “Honest adaptive confidence bands and self-similar functions.”

title: Policy-value inference after learning under interference
open: Obtain valid confidence bounds for the value of a learned treatment-allocation policy when one person’s treatment affects others and the policy is selected using the same network data.
status: Policy learning and randomization-based interference inference have substantial separate literatures. Their joint post-selection problem is more demanding.
why: It would support defensible rollout of network-wide interventions.
key_works: Aronow and Samii, 2017, “Estimating Average Causal Effects Under General Interference, with Application to a Social Network Experiment,” arXiv:1305.6156; Athey and Wager, 2021, “Policy Learning With Observational Data.”

title: Learning the exposure mapping
open: Identify or partially identify causal effects when the mapping from neighbors’ treatment assignments to an individual’s effective exposure is unknown and must be learned.
status: General-interference frameworks often specify an exposure mapping. Estimating that mapping without invalidating inference is a distinct unresolved component.
why: It would reduce dependence on arbitrary definitions of spillover exposure.
key_works: Aronow and Samii, 2017, “Estimating Average Causal Effects Under General Interference,” arXiv:1305.6156.

title: Sharp bounds for interacting multiple mediators
open: Obtain computable sharp bounds for mechanism-specific effects when multiple mediators interact, their ordering is partly unknown, and mediator–outcome confounding cannot be excluded.
status: Mediation estimands and identification strategies are established. The target combines uncertain ordering, interactions, and explicit partial identification.
why: It would help distinguish plausible mechanisms without pretending all pathway assumptions are known.
key_works: VanderWeele, 2015, *Explanation in Causal Inference: Methods for Mediation and Interaction*; Cinelli et al., 2025, “A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference,” arXiv:2508.17099.

title: Switchback experiments with unknown carryover
open: Jointly choose switching schedules and estimate treatment effects when carryover duration is unknown, potentially heterogeneous, and comparable to the experimental horizon.
status: Online experimentation has developed many specialized designs. Unknown carryover makes both randomization choice and uncertainty calibration harder.
why: It would improve experiments in marketplaces, logistics, and shared infrastructure.
key_works: Larsen et al., 2024, “Statistical challenges in online controlled experiments: A review of A/B testing methodology,” *The American Statistician* 78:135–149.

title: Downstream inference with uncertain entity linkage
subfield: Missing data, measurement error, and record linkage
open: Produce confidence intervals for regression and causal estimands that integrate uncertainty over possible record linkages, including dependence between linkage quality and the outcome.
status: Probabilistic linkage and entity resolution are mature topics. Treating one estimated linkage as truth can omit a material source of uncertainty.
why: It would improve the reliability of linked administrative and health records.
key_works: Binette and Steorts, 2022, “(Almost) All of Entity Resolution,” arXiv:2008.04443, DOI:10.1126/sciadv.abi8021.

title: Imputation valid for adaptively chosen analyses
subfield: Missing data, measurement error, and record linkage
open: Develop imputation procedures and uncertainty rules that remain valid for a declared class of downstream analyses selected after inspecting the imputed data.
status: Proposed target extending congeniality and adaptive-analysis concerns. Validity for one prespecified analysis does not establish validity for an unrestricted analytic search.
why: It would make reusable completed datasets less likely to produce undercovered conclusions.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow,” arXiv:2011.01808.

title: Efficient sample-optimal pure-private sparse means
open: Achieve information-theoretically optimal sample complexity for pure differentially private sparse Gaussian mean estimation with a polynomial-time algorithm, or establish a matching computational barrier.
status: Explicitly highlighted in the 2025 robust-statistics open-problem lecture; privacy-induced computational gaps are established in related sparse estimation settings.
why: It would make strong privacy practical for high-dimensional population estimation.
key_works: Georgiev and Hopkins, 2022, “Privacy Induces Robustness: Information-Computation Gaps and Sparse Mean Estimation,” arXiv:2211.00724; UW CSE 599K, 2025, “Lecture 18.”

title: Change-point intervals after choosing the number of changes
open: Construct simultaneous location intervals that remain valid after data-driven selection of the number, scale, and type of changes under dependent noise.
status: Sharp localization theory exists for important independent mean-change models. Full post-selection coverage is a stronger requirement.
why: It would attach defensible dates to inferred regime changes.
key_works: Wang, Yu, and Rinaldo, 2018/2020, “Univariate Mean Change Point Detection: Penalization, CUSUM and Optimality,” arXiv:1810.09498; Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference.”

title: Computational limits of covariance change detection
open: Determine statistical and polynomial-time detection boundaries for sparse covariance changes when both the pre-change covariance and change time are unknown.
status: Proposed target connecting high-dimensional change detection and sparse spectral hardness. Mean-change theory alone does not characterize this problem.
why: It would reveal when monitoring altered relationships requires more data than detecting altered averages.
key_works: Berthet and Rigollet, 2013, “Complexity Theoretic Lower Bounds for Sparse Principal Component Detection”; Wang et al., “Univariate Mean Change Point Detection,” arXiv:1810.09498.

title: Microergodicity in nonstationary anisotropic models
open: Classify which covariance functionals are consistently identifiable under fixed-domain asymptotics for useful nonstationary, anisotropic, and multivariate spatial models.
status: Microergodic parameters are understood in important stationary families. Generalizing the identifiable parameter, rather than assuming all covariance parameters are estimable, remains essential.
why: It would stop spatial models from attaching artificial certainty to nonidentifiable parameters.
key_works: Zhang, Tang, and Banerjee, 2024, “Fixed-Domain Asymptotics Under Vecchia’s Approximation of Spatial Process Likelihoods”; Moraga, 2023, *Spatial Statistics for Data Science: Theory and Practice with R*.

title: Honest adaptation across tail classes
open: Characterize when confidence intervals for extreme quantiles can adapt to unknown tail class and second-order bias without losing uniform coverage.
status: Proposed frontier formulation. Adaptation must confront indistinguishability between distributions that agree over observed ranges but differ in remote tails.
why: It would improve the credibility of rare-risk extrapolation.
key_works: Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes,” arXiv:2004.12182; Bull, 2012, “Honest adaptive confidence bands and self-similar functions.”

title: Graphs mixing asymptotic dependence and independence
open: Build identifiable sparse multivariate tail models that accommodate different pairs or subsets exhibiting asymptotic dependence or asymptotic independence, with valid structure uncertainty.
status: Sparse extremal models are well developed in important regimes. Combining regimes without incoherent joint distributions is a continuing frontier.
why: It would better represent compound risks that do not share one universal tail-dependence pattern.
key_works: Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes,” arXiv:2004.12182.

title: Efficient inference in hard stochastic-block-model phases
open: Resolve the polynomial-time detectability frontier in sparse block models with sufficiently many groups where information-theoretic and algorithmic thresholds separate.
status: Thresholds are settled in important two-community and other special regimes. Those successes do not eliminate the harder multi-community phases.
why: It would clarify when network community information is present but computationally inaccessible.
key_works: Abbe, 2017/2018, “Community Detection and Stochastic Block Models: Recent Developments,” arXiv:1703.10146.

title: Uncertainty for overlapping multilayer communities
open: Infer the number, overlap, and cross-layer alignment of communities with calibrated uncertainty when layers differ in sparsity and share only some nodes.
status: Proposed target extending block-model and shared-subspace methods. Fixed community count and complete layer alignment are materially easier.
why: It would make multilayer community findings less dependent on arbitrary modeling choices.
key_works: Abbe, “Community Detection and Stochastic Block Models”; Lock et al., 2013, “Joint and individual variation explained,” arXiv:1102.4110.

title: Functional regression with unknown ill-posedness
open: Obtain honest adaptive inference for functional regression coefficients when predictor covariance eigenvalue decay and coefficient smoothness are both unknown.
status: Estimation and regularization theory provide a baseline. Simultaneous adaptation of uncertainty to unknown ill-posedness is more restrictive.
why: It would make functional regression error bars less dependent on fixed truncation assumptions.
key_works: Morris, 2015, “Functional Regression,” arXiv:1406.4068; Ray, “Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise,” arXiv:1407.3397.

title: Minimax conditional-independence testing for functional data
open: Establish sharp testing rates for conditional independence among random functions under explicit spectral and smoothness restrictions, including adaptation to unknown effective dimension.
status: Hilbert-space conditional-independence methods exist. The target is an optimal, adaptive theory rather than unrestricted testing, which faces impossibility.
why: It would strengthen functional graphical models and dynamic biological pathway analysis.
key_works: Shah and Peters, 2020, “The Hardness of Conditional Independence Testing and the Generalised Covariance Measure,” arXiv:1804.07203; Lundborg et al., 2022, Hilbert-space conditional-independence work, DOI:10.1111/rssb.12544.

title: Multistate models with informative intermittent observation
open: Infer transition intensities and state-occupation probabilities when states are observed intermittently, visit timing depends on hidden state, and recurrent transitions may be missed.
status: Multistate and recurrent-event models provide a foundation. Jointly modeling informative observation and unobserved transitions remains a demanding extension.
why: It would improve analysis of disease progression and repairable systems.
key_works: Andersen and Keiding, 2002, “Multistate models for event history analysis”; Beyersmann et al., 2012, *Competing Risks and Multistate Models with R*.

title: Fine-mapping uncertainty under LD-reference mismatch
subfield: Statistical genetics, omics, and microbiome analysis
open: Construct credible or confidence sets for causal variants that remain calibrated when reference linkage disequilibrium differs from the study population and rare variants are incompletely represented.
status: Statistical fine-mapping is mature, but reference mismatch and unresolved correlated variants remain important limitations.
why: It would improve the reliability of variant prioritization for biological experiments.
key_works: Schaid, Chen, and Larson, 2018, “From genome-wide associations to candidate causal variants by statistical fine-mapping,” DOI:10.1038/s41576-018-0016-z.

title: Cross-population polygenic-score uncertainty
subfield: Statistical genetics, omics, and microbiome analysis
open: Quantify individual and subgroup prediction uncertainty when polygenic scores transfer across populations with different allele frequencies, linkage patterns, environments, and ascertainment.
status: Transferability and unequal predictive performance are documented. The target is calibrated uncertainty and transport diagnostics, not merely improved average accuracy.
why: It would make genetic prediction less likely to amplify unequal evidential support.
key_works: Martin et al., 2019, “Clinical use of current polygenic risk scores may exacerbate health disparities,” DOI:10.1038/s41588-019-0379-x.

title: Barker sequences longer than thirteen
open: Prove that no binary Barker sequence has length greater than thirteen, or construct one.
status: Odd lengths beyond thirteen are excluded; the unresolved even-length case is connected to circulant Hadamard matrices. Large numerical exclusions do not settle all lengths.
why: It would resolve an extremal low-autocorrelation design problem.
key_works: Turyn and Storer, 1961, “On binary sequences”; Leung and Schmidt, 2005, “The field descent method”; Leung and Schmidt, 2012, “New restrictions on possible orders of circulant Hadamard matrices.”

title: Projective plane of order twelve
open: Determine whether a finite projective plane of order twelve exists; equivalently, whether a symmetric \(2\!-\!(157,13,1)\) design exists.
status: A classical unresolved finite-geometry existence problem. Necessary arithmetic conditions do not rule out order twelve.
why: It would clarify the limits of highly balanced incidence designs.
key_works: Elkies, 2015, Harvard Math 155 finite-geometry notes; classical projective-plane and balanced-design literature.

title: Full transversals in odd-order Latin squares
open: Prove or disprove that every Latin square of odd order has a transversal containing one cell from every row, every column, and every symbol.
status: A longstanding full-transversal conjecture. Results about near-transversals do not settle the full odd-order statement.
why: It would strengthen existence guarantees for balanced selections in combinatorial designs.
key_works: Ryser, 1967, formulation; Wanless, 2011, “Transversals in Latin squares: a survey” (verify bibliographic details); Wanless, “Data on transversals in Latin squares.”

title: Hadamard matrices of every admissible order
open: Prove or disprove that a Hadamard matrix exists for every positive order divisible by four.
status: A classical unresolved existence conjecture with many infinite constructions and extensive computational progress. Historical lists of the smallest missing orders should not be treated as current records.
why: It would complete a basic existence foundation for orthogonal two-level designs and coding constructions.
key_works: Hadamard, 1893, determinant work; “Quaternionic Perfect Sequences and Hadamard Matrices,” 2026, arXiv:2601.22337; OEIS A007299 for evolving existence records.

title: Nonexistence of larger circulant Hadamard matrices
open: Prove or disprove that the only nontrivial circulant Hadamard matrices have order four.
status: A longstanding conjecture. Strong arithmetic restrictions exclude many possible orders but do not constitute an all-orders proof.
why: It would settle a highly structured class of orthogonal sequence designs.
key_works: Leung and Schmidt, 2012, “New restrictions on possible orders of circulant Hadamard matrices,” DOI:10.1007/s10623-011-9493-1; “Quaternionic Perfect Sequences and Hadamard Matrices,” 2026, arXiv:2601.22337.
aliases: Circulant Hadamard conjecture; Ryser’s circulant Hadamard conjecture.

title: Three mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order ten
open: Construct three pairwise mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order ten, or prove that no such triple exists.
status: A specific longstanding design problem. Recent SAT work resolves restricted structural cases, not the unrestricted triple-existence question.
why: It would advance exact small-design existence and constraint-solving methods.
key_works: Myrvold, 1999, “Negative results for orthogonal triples of Latin squares of order 10”; Bright, Keita, and Stevens, 2026, “Myrvold’s results on orthogonal triples of 10×10 Latin squares: A SAT investigation,” DOI:10.37236/13960; “Improving SAT Solvers on Orthogonal Latin Square Problems,” 2026, arXiv:2605.02132.

title: SIC measurements in every complex dimension
subfield: Optimal transport, topology, and geometric statistics
open: Prove or disprove that every complex dimension \(d\) admits \(d^2\) equiangular unit vectors defining a symmetric informationally complete quantum measurement.
status: Formulated in the late 1990s; many constructions and numerical solutions exist, but an unconditional all-dimensions theorem remains open in the 2026 problem collection.
why: It would settle the existence of highly symmetric measurement designs for quantum-state estimation.
key_works: Zauner, 1999, doctoral thesis; Zauner, 2011, “Quantum designs: Foundations of a non-commutative design theory”; Bandeira et al., 2026, “Randomstrasse 101: Open Problems of 2025,” arXiv:2603.29571.

title: Tenfold cheaper physical reliability qualification
open: Reduce physical test expenditure by at least 10× while matching preregistered reliability bounds and out-of-condition validation performance, using justified simulation and accelerated testing.
status: Proposed moonshot. Savings must include simulator development, calibration specimens, and the cost of failed qualification attempts.
why: It would accelerate product development without weakening reliability evidence.
key_works: Hong, Zhang, and Meeker, 2018, “Big Data and Reliability Applications: The Complexity Dimension”; Cranmer et al., 2020, “The frontier of simulation-based inference.”

title: Log-free resilient cores under covariance bounds
open: Determine whether \(O(d/\epsilon)\) samples from every mean-zero distribution with covariance bounded by the identity contain a \((1-\epsilon)\)-fraction subset with universally bounded empirical second moment, with constant high probability.
status: Explicitly listed in a 2025 robust-statistics open-problem lecture; the comparison bound includes an additional logarithmic dimension factor.
why: It would sharpen the sample foundations of robust estimation.
key_works: University of Washington CSE 599K, 2025, “Lecture 18: Some open problems in robust statistics (and friends),” December 1.
